title: Affine morphisms over quasi-affine schemes and their canonical affinization square
statement: Let $f:P\to Q$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $Q$ is quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Then $P$ is quasi-affine. Write $C=\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$, $D=\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_Q)$, and $f^*:D\to C$ for pullback of sections. Let $j_P:P\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $j_Q:Q\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be the canonical morphisms corresponding to the identity maps on sections [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and the square with top arrow $j_P$, left arrow $f$, right arrow $\operatorname{Spec}(f^*)$ and bottom arrow $j_Q$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular $(\operatorname{Spec}(f^*))^{-1}(j_Q(Q))=j_P(P)$ as open subschemes of $\operatorname{Spec}C$.
